tally.headline: 2 of 3 gradeable claims held up, 1 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 11 points toward Ole Miss of the quote EdgeDesk captured at captured (stale 146h) · DraftKings. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 55.4 sat 3.1 points below the captured total of 58.5.

closing_line.note: The line moved 5 points toward the side EdgeDesk’s number leaned before kickoff. That is the market arriving where EdgeDesk already was, and over many games it is the only evidence that a disagreement carried information.

reasons: 1 of 1 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 8.5 and the game finished 8 the home way — 0.5 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

verdict.line: THE NUMBER LANDED AND THE REASONING DID NOT. This is the most dangerous result on this page, because it pays and teaches nothing. Nothing below should be read as EdgeDesk having understood this game.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: LSU holds the largest measured edge in this matchup: LSU 59.5 (#8 of 67) vs Ole Miss 47.0 (#44 of 67) — 36 places on the national board.
lessons.actual_result: LSU Tigers 5.85 yards per pass attempt against Ole Miss Rebels 7.56; LSU Tigers 158 net passing yards against Ole Miss Rebels 363.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named LSU as better in passing and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 9 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 8 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, special_teams.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.actual_result: It graded a win. The reasoning behind it did not hold: 1 of 1 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
lessons.lesson: A winning number built on a reading the game contradicted. Nothing about this result should increase confidence in the mechanism EdgeDesk named, and treating it as confirmation is how a model gets worse while its record gets better.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Why did the number land while the mechanism failed? Either the number was right for a reason EdgeDesk has not identified, or it was luck. Both are worth knowing and they are different.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Ole Miss -8.5 where the market has Ole Miss +2.5 at captured (stale 157h) · DraftKings — a 11.0 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Ole Miss Rebels won by 8. the result landed on EdgeDesk’s side of the market number: Ole Miss Rebels beat a margin of -2.5
lessons.lesson: The disagreement landed. One landing proves nothing on its own; the aggregate of them, held against the closing line, is the only thing that would.
